summary:
TerraScope is an interactive web platform developed for NASA's challenge, "Be an Earth System Trend Detective!" It helps users explore how environmental conditions change across different locations and time periods. Using NASA POWER data, TerraScope analyzes variables such as air temperature, precipitation and soil moisture, presenting the results through interactive maps, visualizations and trend comparisons.

Instead of making users interpret complex scientific datasets on their own, TerraScope turns environmental information into understandable insights. Users can explore regions, compare environmental trends and identify areas experiencing significant changes.

Our project aims to make Earth science more accessible, encourage environmental awareness and help people understand what is happening to our planet. We believe that making scientific data easier to explore is an important step towards building a more informed and environmentally conscious community.
details:
TerraScope is a web-based platform that helps people explore how Earth's environmental conditions change over time and across different locations. Users can select a region, explore variables such as temperature, rainfall and soil moisture, and understand their trends through interactive maps and visualizations.

We use NASA POWER data along with geographical boundary datasets to process and analyze environmental changes. Our goal is to make scientific data easier to understand and help people discover patterns in their own regions.

What makes TerraScope different is its location-based approach, allowing users to explore environmental changes geographically rather than just looking at numbers and graphs.

We developed the project using Python, Flask, JavaScript, HTML and CSS, with Leaflet for interactive maps. We also used GitHub for collaboration and AI-assisted tools such as ChatGPT and Google Antigravity during development.

As a team of students, we considered data reliability, geographical accuracy, usability and accessibility. More than anything, we wanted to create something that helps people become curious about our changing planet and encourages them to explore environmental data themselves.
